summary.title: Three lifts
summary.text: Squat, bench press and deadlift in that order at every official competition.

summary.title: Three attempts
summary.text: Each lift allows up to three attempts. The total is built from the best valid attempt of each.

summary.title: Judging panel
summary.text: Three referees on the platform. When in doubt, the decision favors the lifter.

summary.title: Official weigh-in
summary.text: The athlete competes in the body weight class declared at the event weigh-in.

cards.title: Lifts and formats
cards.text: Full Power (squat, bench press, deadlift), Push-Pull (bench press and deadlift), and Squat Only, Bench Press Only, or Deadlift Only, always in the squat → bench press → deadlift sequence.

cards.title: Drug Tested and Non-Tested divisions
cards.text: Competitions can be sanctioned as Drug Tested, Non-Tested, or Both; PLU also recognizes the Gender Neutral (N) Division and the Parasports Division for adaptive athletes.

cards.title: Defining winners
cards.text: First place goes to the highest valid total within division, equipment category, weight class and age group. Best Lifter is decided by DOTS coefficient (McCulloch formula for Masters).

cards.title: Teams
cards.text: Teams of 4 to 15 registered lifters, scored on the average of the team's top 5 DOTS scores, uniform equipment category (Raw, Raw With Wraps, Single-Ply or Multi-Ply), minimum 3 teams for awards.

cards.title: Records
cards.text: Recorded by the Powerlifting United Official Records Chair; a new record must exceed the previous one by at least 0.5 kg and is validated after an on-platform equipment check.

cards.title: Membership in Powerlifting United
cards.text: Athletes, referees and officials must be active PLU members at the time of weigh-in. Membership is paid annually, is non-refundable and non-transferable, and auto-renews every 12 months.

cards.title: Scales
cards.text: Digital, calibrated in kilograms and recertified every 2 years; a minimum of two scales must be available, with at least one rated for 250 kg or more.

cards.title: Platform
cards.text: Between 8×8 and 12×12 feet, no more than 3 inches above the surrounding floor, with a one-piece carpet surface over at least two layers of plywood.

cards.title: Bars and collars
cards.text: Factory-made bars 2.2–2.5 m long (2.4 m max for deadlift bars), 27–32 mm in diameter, weighing 25, 30 or 35 kg; collars weighing 2.5 kg each with a rotating lock mechanism.

cards.title: Competition discs/plates
cards.text: Factory-manufactured, within 0.25% or 10 g of nominal weight, ranging from 0.25 to 25 kg (plus 50 kg plates available), with standardized colors and loading order.

cards.title: Squat racks
cards.text: Hydraulic monolift or a standard powerlifting combo rack, adjustable between 1.00 and 1.70 m in 5 cm increments.

cards.title: Bench
cards.text: Sturdy construction meeting official dimensions (minimum 1.22 m length, uprights adjustable 75–110 cm) with adjustable fail-safe catches.

cards.title: Judging lights and card system
cards.text: Three white and three red lights, one per referee, plus a color-card system: red (position), blue (technical), yellow (commands/other), for transparent judging.

cards.title: Clocks and timers
cards.text: A mandatory 60-second attempt clock at every level of competition, a conditional rest timer for flights under 10 lifters, and a 60-second submission timer.

cards.title: Singlet
cards.text: A single piece, form-fitting, made of fabric that provides no additional support; straps must stay on the shoulders at all times. Applies to raw and raw-with-wraps lifters. See Chapter VII for equipped.

cards.title: T-shirt
cards.text: A cotton-blend shirt with no buttons or reinforced seams, required under the singlet for squat and bench press; optional for deadlift.

cards.title: Underwear and socks
cards.text: Legless briefs of cotton, nylon or polyester (not mandatory), and only one pair of socks per lifter.

cards.title: Belt and footwear
cards.text: Personal equipment allowed within the width, thickness and material specifications of the official rulebook.

cards.title: Wrist wraps and knee sleeves
cards.text: Wraps and sleeves allowed within approved lengths and materials; must be worn over the sleeve when a full bodysuit is used.

cards.title: Non-supportive bandages
cards.text: The lifter must be able to put on and adjust their own personal equipment without outside assistance on the platform.

cards.title: Inspection of personal equipment
cards.text: All personal equipment is inspected before competition to confirm it meets approved specifications.

cards.title: Bodily fluid management
cards.text: Blood or skin particles on the bar or platform must be cleaned immediately before competition continues.

cards.title: The round system
cards.text: Flights of up to 15 lifters; all squat attempts finish for the flight before bench press begins, and bench press before deadlift. Minimum weight change: 2.5 kg. No fourth attempts allowed.

cards.title: The officials
cards.text: Announcer, Meet Director, jury of appeals, timekeeper and official scorers, each with defined responsibilities during the flight.

cards.title: General rules
cards.text: The head referee controls bar loading and platform order; three failed attempts on a given lift disqualify the athlete from that lift.

cards.title: Minor oversight, infractions and cheating
cards.text: The rulebook distinguishes correctable minor oversights, infractions that must be fixed before lifting, and deliberate cheating, each with its own disciplinary handling.

cards.title: Weigh-in window
cards.text: Held within 24 hours before competition, in a private setting; the athlete may weigh in nude, in underwear, or in a singlet.

cards.title: Minor lifter protocol
cards.text: Lifters under 18 weigh in wearing a singlet (200 g is deducted) and require their legal guardian plus two officials of the same sex present.

cards.title: Official record
cards.text: Weight, division, category and athlete data are logged on the official card and entered into LiftingCast, signed by the athlete and the weigh-in official.

cards.title: Equipment check
cards.text: Before or after weigh-in, a Powerlifting United official inspects the athlete's personal equipment against the Chapter III specifications.

lifts.title: Squat
points: The head referee gives the squat and rack commands.
The lifter must meet the required depth and final position.
Grounds for disqualification are detailed in the official PDF.

lifts.title: Bench Press
points: Referee commands: start, press and rack.
The bar must touch the chest or abdomen and return to the starting position.
Buttocks in contact with the bench; feet on the platform.

lifts.title: Deadlift
points: There is no start command: the attempt must begin before the clock expires.
Final position with shoulders, hips and knees fully extended.
The head referee gives the down command to lower the bar.

cards.title: Single-Ply
cards.text: A single-layer-fabric squat/deadlift suit and bench shirt, with seam and material specifications detailed in the official rulebook.

cards.title: Multi-Ply
cards.text: A multi-layer-fabric squat/deadlift suit; a compression/erector shirt and briefs may be worn, and a three-person lift-off is allowed depending on category.

cards.title: Unlimited
cards.text: A division allowing bench shirts with no layer limit; a t-shirt underneath is not required, and all other equipment rules remain unchanged.

canon.text: Three attempts per lift: squat, bench press and deadlift. The official total uses the best valid attempt of each.
The sequence is fixed at every competition: squat, bench press, deadlift.
Three referees judge every attempt on the platform. When in doubt, the decision favors the lifter.
The head referee gives the verbal commands and hand signals for start, press/rack, or down depending on the lift.
The athlete competes in the body weight class declared at the event's official weigh-in.
Appeals of a 2–1 decision must be filed within 60 seconds of the attempt.

Level 1 referee requirements: Provincial Chair approval, a completed background check, the online and in-person practical exams, a minimum of 3 sanctioned events competed in, age 18 or older, and referee at least once every 365 days.
Level 2 (National) referee requirements: a minimum of 1 year of referee experience and a completed competency catalog (flights judged, scoring control, spotting/loading and weigh-ins).

cards.title: Definition
cards.text: Modifying lifting technique or equipment for athletes with a disability or other limitation: adapted benches, prosthetic hooks, or hand signals, among other adaptations.

cards.title: Eligibility and certification
cards.text: Requested at adaptive@powerliftingunited.com; each case is reviewed and a certification of adapted equipment is issued for use on the platform.

cards.title: Competition categories
cards.text: With certified equipment, the athlete may compete in every category, division, class and lift, with no additional restrictions.

cards.title: Safety and assistance
cards.text: Assistance is allowed to move, set up and center the weight; not to start or complete the lift. There is no attempt clock for these lifters.

cards.title: Responsibilities
cards.text: The lifter must obtain certification at least two weeks in advance; the Meet Director and coaches must know and accommodate certified adaptations.

cards.title: Anti-discrimination policy
cards.text: Zero tolerance for discrimination or harassment based on disability or impairment; complaints go to support@powerliftingunited.com and are answered within 5 business days.

cards.title: Background check policy
cards.text: All staff, directors and officials undergo a criminal background check; violent, sexual, or child-related offenses result in automatic termination from PLU.

cards.title: Banned substances list
cards.text: Categories of substances not permitted in drug-tested divisions (anabolic steroids, peptide hormones, stimulants, diuretics and masking agents, among others), full list in the official PDF, pages 66–67.

cards.title: Appendices
cards.text: Appendix A: record request form. Appendix B: Code of Conduct for members, referees and officials of Powerlifting United.
